title: GCP Cloud API Error Rate Spike

compliance.assurance_rationale: Saved search evidence for AU-2 when alert outputs are archived.
compliance.controlObjective: Evidence that NIST-800-53 AU-2 (Event logging) is enforced — Splunk UC-4.4.73: GCP Cloud API Error Rate Spike.
compliance.evidenceArtifact: Saved search 'UC-4.4.73' running on sourcetype google:gcp:audit and supporting catalogue-defined data sources, archived to the restricted audit_evidence index (default 7-year retention). Auto-drafted — SME review required.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay a burst of `google:gcp:audit` events with a non-zero `protoPayload.status.code` (for example 7 PERMISSION_DENIED or 8 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED) into `index=gcp`. GCP AuditLog failures use that status code, not the CloudTrail field `errorCode`. The saved search still filters `errorCode="*"`, so this replay returns zero rows until the search is retargeted.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay normal-volume `google:gcp:audit` traffic whose `protoPayload.status.code` is 0 or absent. A single failure event is not a rate spike. The saved search still filters `errorCode`, so it does not measure this condition.

dataSources: `index=gcp` sourcetype=`google:gcp:pubsub:audit:admin_activity` or `google:gcp:pubsub:audit:data_access` (or `google:gcp:pubsub:message` before add-on 4.0.0) collected via Splunk cloud TA for GCP; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

description: UC-4.4.73 — GCP Cloud API Error Rate Spike: GCP AuditLog failures are `protoPayload.status.code` (a google.rpc.Code integer) plus `status.message`. The saved search still filters `errorCode="*"`, which is an AWS CloudTrail field, so it does not match real audit failures until it is retargeted.
value: On Google Cloud, detecting 'GCP Cloud API Error Rate Spike' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.4.73 drives high-priority operations alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:audit.
visualization: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report.
knownFalsePositives: Approved change windows; documented automation service principals; sandbox accounts excluded via lookup.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=gcp`.
• Install and configure Splunk cloud TA for GCP with the modular input for `google:gcp:audit`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `protoPayload.methodName` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:audit.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:audit" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
GCP audit failures sit in `protoPayload.status.code`. The search below still filters `errorCode`, a CloudTrail field, and returns no GCP failures until it is retargeted.
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:audit" errorCode="*"
| table _time protoPayload.methodName protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail resourceName
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.73_gcp_cloud_api_error_rate_73"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `google:gcp:audit` in `index=gcp` to detect gcp cloud api error rate spike. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the GCP Logs Explorer console for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `protoPayload.methodName` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_73_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk cloud TA for GCP and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
